overview: 48ft Traditional Narrowboat – Project with Great Potential A fantastic opportunity to create your own boat with this 48ft traditional stern narrowboat, built by Teddesley Boats in 1977. Spacious, clean and open-plan inside with a fitted galley, shower room with cassette toilet and solid fuel stove. Powered by a characterful 3-cylinder air-cooled Lister diesel engine which runs well. The cabin sides and roof have recently been repainted, providing a great starting point for the new owner to complete the interior to their own taste. An ideal project for the skilled DIYer or enthusiastic amateur and a very affordable entry into life on the water, whether as a leisure boat or potential liveaboard. Plenty of space, plenty of character and bags of potential.

overview: Sentinel is a characterful 70ft traditional narrowboat built in 1976 by Brian Duvall and powered by the much-admired Bolinder engine, perfectly complementing her classic lines and timeless appeal. Stepping aboard from the bow, you are welcomed into a spacious saloon, followed by a well-equipped walkthrough galley featuring a freestanding cooker, washing machine, fridge freezer and ample storage. The light and airy main bedroom offers a comfortable retreat, while the impressive engine room houses the iconic Bolinder engine and generator enabling life aboard to be completely self sufficient. Completing the accommodation is a traditional boatman’s cabin with a single berth, full of charm and surprisingly spacious. Sentinel is a rare opportunity to own a traditional narrowboat with an abundance of character and heritage.
